name: Executive Brief
description: A tight, decision-oriented brief for someone who has two minutes.
outline: Write for a busy reader who was not present: lead with the conclusion or the ask.
Give at most five bullet points of background, each one line.
State the decisions made and the decisions still needed, separately.
List risks or blockers briefly, with who is affected.
End with the single most important next step and its owner if one was named.
Keep it factual: never add information that is not in the transcript, and omit a section when nothing applies.
example:
## Bottom Line
Approve the vendor switch by Friday or the launch slips.

## Next Step
Finance signs off (Priya).
